files.description: Playwright tests for the photo gallery: image/video loading, year filtering, pagination, the timeline view (day sections, infinite-scroll streaming, date scrubber, saved view preference, filters), and the responsive suite. Home is the reference implementation of the shared shell, so the peer-panel contract, narrow Menu, first-paint closed state, applied-filter badge, mobile pagination row, filter configurator dialog, touch reordering, RTL/zoom/short-landscape, the built-in theme matrix and the app-wide panel registration audit are asserted here, alongside the gallery's own timeline jump control, rotation-safe streaming and coarse-pointer card affordances.

testContext: The tests rely on the following selectors: `.photo-grid` for the main gallery container, `.photo-card` for individual photo items, `.photo-date` for the card date, and role locators for buttons/links like `getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply Filters' })` and `getByRole('link', { name: 'Next ›' })`. IMPORTANT: every ` so Apply Filters keeps view=timeline in the URL. RESPONSIVE (2026-08-30): shared assertions come from generated_tests/_support/responsive.ts (expectNoPageOverflow, expectRouteFits, expectFitsViewport, expectPanelContract, withTouchContext, touchDrag, CONTRACT_WIDTHS, VIEWPORTS) - never re-implement them. Home registers one panel, `home-filters` (button `#home-filters-toggle`, host `#navbar-context-panels`); the narrow breakpoint nav.js uses is max-width 1200px. The pagination controls carry an aria-label, which overrides their visible "Next ›" text as the accessible name. On narrow/coarse screens the timeline scrubber rail is replaced by `.timeline-jump` year links (`.timeline-jump-year`), which stick under the navbar; the sticky day headers offset by both. Built-in themes are exercised by swapping the `link[href*="/theme.css"]` href (with a cache-busting param) rather than changing the app-wide default.
explanation: 2026-07-18: Added 5 timeline-view tests (day sections/month dividers, infinite scroll via the htmx sentinel with continuation-merge assertions, scrubber density bars + pointer jump to #month anchor, server-side view-preference persistence, filters in timeline view) and made the whole file deterministic against the server-global library_view preference: test.describe.configure({ mode: "default" }) serializes the file, every navigation passes explicit ?view= (beforeEach now goes to /?view=grid, the video test to /?media-type=video&view=grid), and the persistence/filter tests restore /?view=grid when done. All 9 tests pass against the isolated sandbox. The responsive block adds the shell contract on Home plus the gallery's own narrow-screen behaviour; every fixed responsive defect carries a REGRESSION comment naming its cause.
